claims.text: Adding approximately 1 atomic percent boron before rapid solidification will improve the glass-forming ability of a phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy relative to an undoped baseline.
Adding approximately 1 atomic percent boron will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to an undoped baseline.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of approximately 1 atomic percent boron into the melt before rapid solidification.
Boron will enhance atomic-packing frustration in the alloy.
Boron will increase local chemical heterogeneity in the alloy.
Boron atoms have a small atomic size in the relevant alloy context.
Boron atoms have limited diffusivity in the relevant alloy melt or undercooled liquid.
Boron will disrupt atomic diffusion during cooling.
Boron will suppress nucleation during cooling.
Suppression of diffusion and nucleation will delay crystallization and facilitate retention of the amorphous state.
The boron-doped alloy will exhibit a larger critical casting thickness than the undoped alloy.
The boron-doped alloy will exhibit a higher onset crystallization temperature than the undoped alloy.
The proposed beneficial effect is expected under rapid-solidification conditions.
Whether the intervention remains effective at slower cooling rates is uncertain.
The optimal boron concentration and the magnitudes of the improvements are not yet established.
Doped and undoped samples will be processed under identical rapid-solidification conditions and compared using critical casting thickness and DSC onset crystallization temperature.
